project.name: Worth UI Milestone 3.7 Runtime Topology And Proof-Flow Cleanup Gate

phases.title: Structural Inventory And Concept Freeze
acceptance: inventory names facade leakage, topology sinkhole, helper swamp, authority mixing, function overload, file-size, and test-bypass cleanup targets
inventory classifies each finding by failure mode and names the closeout evidence required
phase freezes cleanup scope and does not broaden into 3.8 runtime behavior
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 1. Produce the structural cleanup map that later phases must consume, and treat this as evidence work rather than feature implementation.
phases.qa_focus: Check that the inventory names load-bearing architectural failures rather than surface ugliness, and that the concept freeze is preserved.

phases.title: Public Facade And Export Grammar Cleanup
phases.owner: worth-ui public runtime and inspection surfaces
acceptance: public exports read by lifecycle capability and authority class rather than alphabet soup or mirrored topology
facades aggregate and route instead of quietly implementing runtime law or diagnostics assembly
external callers can follow one stable lifecycle path without deep-import pressure into internal modules
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 2. Narrow public facades so callers can see valid order and authority without grep archaeology.
phases.qa_focus: Check for business logic in lib.rs or facade roots, leaked helpers, and compatibility exports that preserve accidental structure.

phases.title: Runtime Lifecycle Tree Cleanup
acceptance: runtime tree teaches planning, activation staging, atomic swap, reconciliation, handle allocation, and host observation as visible lanes
same-level file swamps are reduced into understandable lifecycle homes
host-local shortcuts cannot bypass intended runtime lifecycle order after the refactor
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 3. Reshape the runtime tree around lifecycle and authority boundaries rather than flat storage.
phases.qa_focus: Check for dumping-ground roots, renamed-but-unsplit bags, and host/runtime mixing that still hides valid transition order.

phases.title: Evidence And Planning Proof-Flow Topology Cleanup
phases.owner: worth-ui runtime evidence and planning proof flows
acceptance: planning, allocation, and diagnostic evidence are grouped by named transition family rather than one vocabulary warehouse
source authority, denial posture, next capability, and output proof are visible in code shape for major runtime flows
copied receipt fields and predicate-reconstructed transition grammar are eliminated from touched flows
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 4. Turn evidence topology into named transition families instead of a giant noun shelf.
phases.qa_focus: Check for proof theater, receipt copying, transition reconstruction from booleans, and evidence files acting as semantic dumping grounds.

phases.title: Graph, Planning, And Host Seam Cleanup
acceptance: graph, planning, host observation, and Query-facing seams each own one clear responsibility boundary
host code allocates pixels and reports observations without recreating runtime semantic ownership
Worth UI consumes Query-owned public artifacts without restating or rebuilding Query runtime truth locally
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 5. Clean cross-subsystem seams so boundary law is explicit and hard to bypass.
phases.qa_focus: Check for graph/runtime/host role collapse, host-owned semantic meaning, and local reimplementation of Query truth.

phases.title: Inspection, Certification, And Test Authority Cleanup
acceptance: inspection, certification, and test support consume runtime truth instead of becoming alternate authority lanes
production law needed by runtime crates lives in production crates rather than test or certification vocabulary
synthetic proof and harness helpers are visibly labeled as support authority rather than production truth
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 6. Keep inspection and certification as proof consumers rather than letting them become the law.
phases.qa_focus: Check for helper-bypass construction, certification-as-authority, and production code depending on test-only vocabulary.

phases.title: Function Decomposition And Helper Placement Cleanup
phases.owner: worth-ui runtime function and helper shape
acceptance: touched god functions decompose into orchestration plus named semantic steps
helpers live at the narrowest domain responsibility they actually serve
generic helper or support files no longer hide production semantics or parallel implementations
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 7. Split overloaded functions and relocate helpers so the code reads as visible logic hierarchy.
phases.qa_focus: Check for one-body collection-classification-validation-mutation-output mixes, helper sprawl, and names compensating for unclear structure.

phases.title: Structural Closeout And 3.8 Readiness
acceptance: closeout evidence shows cleaned topology, narrowed facades, proof-flow readability, and anti-bypass enforcement appropriate to touched surfaces
3.8 can consume runtime planning and evidence lanes without reopening broad-facade or dumping-ground shape
remaining structural exceptions, if any, are explicit, bounded, and owned
phases.instructions: Implement 3.7 Phase 8. Produce the structural closeout bundle and prove 3.8 can build on cleaned runtime surfaces.
phases.qa_focus: Check that the milestone leaves a genuinely easier-to-reason-about runtime rather than a cosmetically reorganized one.
